NEW YORK (CNN) -- A massive anti-Mafia sweep that stretched from New York to Sicily has not only cut off the head of the Gambino crime family but lopped off "the shoulders and chest" too, prosecutors said Thursday. John "Jackie the Nose" D'Amico, shown in 1992, is one of 62 people indicted. Sixty-two members of the Gambino, Genovese and Bonanno families face 80 charges, ranging from money laundering to illegal gambling and murder. "These charges strike at the very core of the Gambino family," said Benton Campbell, United States attorney for the Eastern District of New York. The Gambino family profited from extortion within the New York construction industry and its labor unions, according to the charges.  Watch the perp walk » . Several companies allegedly paid a "mob tax" in return for "protection" and "permission to operate," said Gordon Heddell, inspector general of the U.S. Department of Labor. Other charges involve an alleged illegal gambling ring, said Richard Brown, Queens County district attorney. Nicholas Corozzo -- a reputed captain in the Gambino family -- was involved in a sports gambling enterprise that relied in part on toll-free telephones, Brown alleged. Meanwhile, four members of the Gambino family are charged with eight crimes involving murder, according to the indictment. Those charges include the felony murder of Jose Delgado Rivera, who was shot and killed in an armored truck during a robbery in 1990. "Today we are able to bring closure to crimes from the past that have never been forgotten," Campbell said. He said the crimes span back over three decades.  Watch feds say they've 'cut off the head' of crime family » . Key to the Gambino arrests Thursday was a member of the Attorney General's Organized Crime Task Force who infiltrated the Gambino family and recorded hundred of hours of conversations, said John Milgrim, a spokesman for the attorney general. Forty-five of those charged are already in custody, police said. Arrests were made in New York City; Long Island, New York; and New Jersey. "It is as unrelenting as weeds that continue to sprout in the cracks of society," New York Attorney General Andrew Cuomo said of organized crime. "We will not rest until organized crime is a distant memory." In addition to the arrests in the New York area, police in Italy detained 77 people in connection with organized crime. Those arrests netted important members of a powerful clan in Sicily linked to Mafia boss Salvatore Lo Piccolo, who was believed to be the successor of the boss of bosses, Bernardo Provenzano.  Watch the prosecutor explain why authorities acted now » . Police say that in his attempt to rise to power, Le Piccolo tried to mend fences with New York-based Mafia families after those ties were broken during the bloody Mafia wars of the 1980s. Those families included the Gambinos of New York and the Inzerillos of Italy. Provenzano was arrested two years ago in Corleone. "It is evident that the intent of the Mafia in Palermo was to re-establish a dialogue through the Inzerillo family in the U.S," Francesco Messineo of the Italian Police said. "A dialogue that was never interrupted because the relationship between the American and the Italian Mafia is historic, based on long tradition. But there was certainly an attempt to re-establish that connection." Investigators believe mob clans wanted to collaborate on illegal commercial ventures such as money laundering and drug trafficking. Italian officials said the arrests were aimed at preventing these illegal activities, but they warned that other Mafia clans in Sicily oppose the return of the Inzerillo family to the island, and therefore were concerned about a new Mafia war. # Federal Anti-Mafia Sweep Nets 62 Organized Crime Figures in Historic Cross-Continental Operation

In one of the most significant blows to organized crime in recent years, a sweeping investigation stretching from New York City to the shores of Sicily has culminated in the indictment of 62 individuals connected to three of America's most notorious crime families: the Gambino, Genovese, and Bonanno organizations. The defendants now face a staggering 80 separate charges, marking this as one of the most comprehensive anti-Mafia prosecutions in recent memory.

## A Wide-Ranging Criminal Enterprise Exposed

The scope of the alleged criminal activity is extensive, painting a picture of deeply entrenched organized crime operations that have persisted for decades. Prosecutors allege that those charged engaged in a diverse array of illegal activities, including money laundering schemes, illegal gambling operations, extortion rackets, and even murder. This broad spectrum of charges strikes directly at the operational core of the Gambino crime family, suggesting investigators successfully penetrated multiple layers of the organization's criminal infrastructure.

## The "Mob Tax": Exploiting New York's Construction Industry

Perhaps most striking among the allegations is the systematic extortion scheme allegedly orchestrated by the Gambino family within New York's construction industry and labor unions. According to investigators, the crime family imposed what has been described as a "mob tax" on construction companies operating throughout the city. Under this alleged scheme, businesses were forced to pay for the "privilege" of conducting operations without interference—essentially purchasing protection from the very criminal organization that would otherwise disrupt their work. This extortion racket reportedly generated substantial illicit profits for the Gambino family while embedding organized crime deeply within a critical sector of New York's economy.

## Murder Charges Span Three Decades

Among the most serious allegations are murder-related charges leveled against four members of the Gambino family. These charges include the 1990 felony murder of Jose Delgado Rivera, who was killed during an armored truck robbery. The inclusion of this decades-old case demonstrates the extensive timeline investigators traced in building their case, with alleged criminal activity dating back more than thirty years. This long historical arc underscores the persistent and enduring nature of the criminal enterprise, as well as the thoroughness of the investigation required to bring such long-standing cases to light.

## The Undercover Operation That Cracked the Case

Central to the success of this massive takedown was the work of an undercover operative from the Attorney General's Organized Crime Task Force. This agent successfully infiltrated the Gambino family's inner circles, gaining access to conversations and dealings that would otherwise have remained hidden from law enforcement. Over an extended period, the undercover operative recorded hundreds of hours of conversations that captured incriminating evidence directly from those involved in the criminal enterprise. This painstaking, high-risk infiltration effort proved instrumental in building the extensive case against the 62 defendants, providing prosecutors with the direct evidence needed to pursue such a wide range of serious charges.

## Conclusion

This operation represents a landmark achievement in the ongoing effort to dismantle organized crime networks that have operated with impunity for generations. By combining international cooperation, meticulous long-term investigation, and daring undercover work, law enforcement agencies have struck a significant blow against three of New York's most powerful crime families, potentially disrupting criminal operations that have plagued the construction industry and labor unions for decades.

# Major Anti-Mafia Sweep Dismantles Gambino Family Structure

In one of the most significant organized crime operations in recent history, federal and Italian authorities announced the indictment of 62 individuals connected to New York's Gambino, Genovese, and Bonanno crime families. The sweeping operation, which stretched across the Atlantic from New York to Sicily, culminated years of painstaking investigative work and resulted in 80 separate charges being filed against the alleged mobsters.

The charges brought against the defendants were extensive and serious, encompassing money laundering, illegal gambling operations, extortion schemes, and murder. The breadth of these charges reflects the wide-ranging criminal enterprise that investigators say these families had built and maintained over decades of operation.

## The Undercover Operation

At the heart of this successful prosecution was an unprecedented undercover investigation. A task force member successfully infiltrated the notoriously secretive Gambino family, gaining the trust necessary to gather crucial evidence from within the organization's inner circles. Over the course of the operation, this undercover operative recorded hundreds of hours of conversations that would prove instrumental in building the case against the alleged criminals.

These recordings reportedly captured incriminating discussions that provided prosecutors with direct evidence of criminal activity, conspiracy, and the inner workings of the crime family's operations—evidence that would be nearly impossible to obtain through traditional investigative methods alone.

## Prosecutors Highlight Historic Significance

Law enforcement officials speaking about the operation emphasized that its impact extended far beyond simply removing a few key figures from power. According to prosecutors, this sweep represented something more comprehensive: the dismantling of the entire operational structure of the Gambino crime family, not merely its leadership.

This distinction is particularly significant in the context of organized crime prosecutions, as historically, the removal of leadership figures has often simply created opportunities for new leaders to emerge and continue criminal operations. By targeting the full operational structure, authorities expressed confidence that this operation could deal a more lasting blow to the organization's ability to function.

## Closure for Decades-Old Crimes

Perhaps most notably, the indictments brought resolution to criminal cases that had remained unsolved for more than thirty years. Among these cold cases was a particularly violent 1990 armored truck robbery that resulted in murder—a crime that had gone unpunished for over three decades until this investigation connected it to the broader criminal network being prosecuted.

This aspect of the case underscores the long-reaching consequences of organized crime investigations, where evidence gathered in present-day operations can illuminate and resolve crimes that occurred years or even decades earlier, finally providing answers and accountability for victims and their families who had waited years for justice.

The scale of this operation, both in terms of geographic reach and the number of individuals charged, represents a significant milestone in ongoing efforts to combat organized crime and demonstrates the continued vulnerability of criminal organizations to sophisticated law enforcement infiltration techniques.

# The Rise of "NEW YORK (CNN)" — A Journalistic Institution

For decades, the byline "NEW YORK (CNN)" has appeared at the top of countless news stories, signaling to readers that they are about to receive reporting filtered through one of America's most influential media organizations, based in one of the world's most dynamic cities.

## The Significance of the Dateline

In journalism, a dateline serves a crucial purpose: it tells readers where a story originates. When CNN reporters file stories from New York, this simple line—NEW YORK (CNN)—carries weight. New York City is the financial capital of the world, home to Wall Street, the United Nations, and countless corporate headquarters. Stories originating from this dateline often cover breaking business news, cultural events, or major announcements that ripple across global markets.

## CNN's New York Presence

While CNN's headquarters are famously located in Atlanta, Georgia, the network maintains a massive operational presence in New York City. Their studios in the Hudson Yards area and elsewhere in Manhattan serve as a hub for:

- Business and financial reporting, given proximity to Wall Street
- Breaking news coverage of events in the tri-state area
- Interviews with prominent figures who are based in or passing through New York
- Coverage of the United Nations and international diplomacy

## Why This Combination Matters

The pairing of these three elements—a specific location, a major city, and a globally recognized news brand—represents something larger than the sum of its parts. It represents the infrastructure of modern information distribution. When millions of people see "NEW YORK (CNN)" at the start of an article, they're witnessing the intersection of:

1. **Geographic credibility** – New York's status as a global nerve center
2. **Institutional trust** – CNN's decades-long reputation (despite varying opinions on media bias)
3. **Immediacy** – The implication that this news is fresh, verified, and worth attention

## Conclusion

Whether covering a stock market plunge, a celebrity scandal, or breaking political news, the formula of NEW YORK, CNN continues to be one of the most recognizable taglines in American journalism—a small string of words that carries an outsized signal about where news comes from and who's telling it.

**Federal Prosecutors Unseal Sweeping Indictment Against Gambino, Genovese and Bonanno Crime Families**

*By CNN Staff*

**NEW YORK (CNN)** — Federal prosecutors in the Eastern District of New York unsealed a sprawling indictment Tuesday charging more than two dozen alleged members and associates of the Gambino, Genovese, and Bonanno organized crime families with racketeering, extortion, loan-sharking, and murder conspiracy charges, in what officials are calling one of the most significant mafia takedowns in decades.

The indictment, the result of a multi-year investigation by the FBI's Organized Crime Task Force in coordination with the New York Police Department and the IRS Criminal Investigation Division, alleges that the three families operated an interconnected criminal enterprise spanning construction fraud, illegal gambling operations, and control of labor unions across the New York metropolitan area.

"For decades, these families have adapted, but they have never disappeared," said the U.S. Attorney for the Eastern District of New York at a news conference outside the federal courthouse in Brooklyn. "Today's charges make clear that traditional organized crime remains a persistent threat to the integrity of our economy and the safety of our communities — and that this office, along with our law enforcement partners, will continue to dismantle it piece by piece."

According to the 87-page indictment, alleged capos and soldiers from the three families coordinated on several fronts, including skimming proceeds from unionized construction sites in Queens and Staten Island, running high-stakes illegal poker operations in Manhattan, and using threats of violence to collect debts tied to a loan-sharking network prosecutors say generated millions of dollars in illicit proceeds annually.

The indictment also alleges that members conspired to murder a rival associate in 2019 following a dispute over control of a waste-management contract, though prosecutors declined to say whether that killing had previously been classified as unsolved.

"This is not nostalgia — this is not 'The Godfather,'" the head of the FBI's New York Field Office said. "This is a modern, adaptive criminal enterprise that has infiltrated legitimate industries, corrupted union officials, and used violence and intimidation to protect its profits. Today, we are sending an unmistakable message: no family, no crew, no code of silence will protect you from federal law enforcement."

Among those named in the indictment are several individuals prosecutors describe as "made members" of the respective families, along with associates allegedly responsible for laundering proceeds through cash-intensive businesses, including restaurants and auto body shops in Brooklyn and Long Island.

Defense attorneys for several of the defendants pushed back on the charges following the announcement. "My client denies these allegations in the strongest possible terms," said one attorney representing a Gambino family associate. "We look forward to confronting this evidence — such as it is — in court."

If convicted on the racketeering conspiracy charges, defendants face up to 20 years in prison, with additional charges — including murder in aid of racketeering — carrying the possibility of life sentences.

Law enforcement officials say the investigation remains ongoing, and additional arrests are possible.

"To anyone who thinks this life still offers protection, still offers a code that shields you from accountability — today should serve as a reminder that it does not," the U.S. Attorney said. "The rules have changed. We follow the money, we follow the evidence, and eventually, we follow it into a courtroom."

Arraignments for the defendants are expected to begin later this week in federal court in Brooklyn.

---

*This story is developing and will be updated.*

**NEW YORK / PALERMO** — Law enforcement agencies in the United States and Italy announced the results of a coordinated anti-Mafia operation this week, leading to multiple arrests in New York and Sicily and shining renewed light on longstanding ties between the Gambino crime family and Sicilian criminal organizations.

## Overview of the Operation

The joint investigation, reportedly built over several years through wiretaps, financial monitoring, and cooperation between the FBI, the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA), Italy's Direzione Investigativa Antimafia (DIA), and Sicilian prosecutors, targeted an alleged network accused of facilitating drug trafficking, money laundering, and extortion across both countries.

Authorities allege the network functioned as a bridge between organized crime figures in New York and Sicilian clans, allowing coordination on financial transactions, the movement of narcotics, and mutual protection arrangements.

## Arrests in New York

In the early morning raids conducted in the New York metropolitan area, federal agents and NYPD officers detained several individuals identified as associates and, in some cases, made members of the Gambino crime family. Charges reportedly include racketeering, conspiracy to distribute narcotics, and money laundering.

Prosecutors from the Eastern District of New York indicated that wiretapped conversations captured discussions referencing counterparts in Sicily, along with coded language believed to relate to shipments and financial transfers.

## Arrests in Sicily

Simultaneously, Italian authorities carried out coordinated raids in Palermo and surrounding towns, arresting individuals linked to Sicilian Mafia clans, some with historical ties to the broader Cosa Nostra structure. Italian investigators say wiretaps and surveillance revealed ongoing contact with contacts in the United States, including discussions of business ventures, family connections, and shared financial interests.

## Alleged Gambino-Sicilian Connections

Investigators emphasized that the Gambino family has long maintained historical and, according to this investigation, continuing links to Sicilian organized crime, dating back to earlier generations of transatlantic Mafia cooperation. Officials say the current case suggests these relationships persisted through informal family ties, business fronts, and periodic communication between figures on both sides of the Atlantic.

According to court documents unsealed as part of the case, conversations intercepted by investigators referenced "old friends" and family relationships spanning multiple decades, which prosecutors argue demonstrates a continued operational relationship rather than a purely symbolic one.

## Official Statements

A spokesperson for the FBI's Organized Crime unit stated that the operation "underscores the enduring nature of Mafia networks and the necessity of continued international cooperation to dismantle them."

Italian officials echoed the sentiment, with a DIA representative noting that "these arrests confirm that traditional criminal alliances have adapted to modern communication and financial systems, but the underlying structures remain remarkably similar to those of past decades."

## What's Next

Suspects arrested in New York are expected to appear in federal court in Brooklyn in the coming days, while those detained in Sicily will face preliminary hearings under Italian law. Authorities on both sides indicated the investigation remains ongoing, with additional arrests possible as financial records and communications continue to be analyzed.

# BREAKING NEWS

## Federal Prosecutors Unseal Sweeping 62-Count Indictment Targeting New York Mafia Families

**NEW YORK** — In one of the largest coordinated law enforcement actions against organized crime in decades, federal prosecutors today unsealed indictments charging 62 alleged members and associates of New York's storied Mafia families with a sprawling range of crimes including murder, extortion, illegal gambling, loansharking, and racketeering.

The early morning arrests, conducted by the FBI in coordination with the NYPD Organized Crime Control Bureau, targeted reputed figures across multiple crime families, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office for the Southern and Eastern Districts of New York. Officials described the operation as the culmination of a multi-year investigation involving wiretaps, confidential informants, and undercover agents.

"These indictments represent a significant blow to organized crime networks that have preyed on businesses, workers, and communities for far too long," said the U.S. Attorney at a press conference this morning. "No one is above the law, regardless of the title they claim within these criminal organizations."

### Charges Span Decades of Alleged Criminal Enterprise

According to the unsealed indictment, defendants face charges under the Racketeer Influenced and Corrupt Organizations (RICO) Act, with prosecutors alleging the defendants operated an ongoing criminal enterprise responsible for:

- **Murder and conspiracy to commit murder**, including at least three unsolved homicides dating back over a decade
- **Extortion** of construction companies, restaurants, and unionized labor sectors
- **Illegal gambling operations**, including sports betting rings and underground poker rooms generating millions in untaxed revenue
- **Loansharking** with predatory interest rates enforced through threats of violence
- **Money laundering** through shell companies and cash-intensive businesses
- **Witness tampering and obstruction of justice**

Prosecutors allege that the criminal enterprise generated tens of millions of dollars in illicit profits, with proceeds allegedly funneled through a network of construction firms, social clubs, and waste management companies in Brooklyn, Staten Island, and parts of Long Island.

### High-Profile Arrests

Among those named in the indictment are several alleged capos and soldiers linked to organized crime families with long histories in the New York metropolitan area. Defense attorneys for several defendants have already signaled they will contest the charges, with one attorney calling the case "a rehash of tired stereotypes wrapped in circumstantial evidence."

Law enforcement officials indicated that cooperating witnesses, including a former high-ranking member turned government informant, played a central role in building the case.
